nina: Heads-up — during vuln triage for a private deployment (customer-omega) we hit an audit gap. keystore-proxy accepted decrypts but there's no corresponding audit event in our splunk stream. @marco any idea?
marco: Yup saw it in the test harness this morning. proxy returns 200 but no decrypt:audit event. looks like events are being swallowed before the sink.
alyssa: Can you paste repro steps / logs?
nina: Repro steps in staging: run the proxy w/ the service account, call /decrypt. Example curl:```
POST /v1/decrypt HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{
  "key_id": "projects/…/keys/rdw-priv",
  "ciphertext": "base64..."
}
```
Log snippet from proxy:```
2025-03-01T10:12:05Z INFO decrypt accepted proxy_id=keystore-proxy-2 request_id=abcd1234
# no matching audit event emitted to splunk for request_id abcd1234
```
jordan: Two quick possibilities — (1) audit sink misconfigured (filtering rules), or (2) RBAC change removed write permission from the SA that emits audit events. also consider netpol/sidecar egress blocking the sink.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy of priv-edge (rev c42) at 2025-03-01T09:00 UTC.
sam: I dug through infra diffs — last week's infra PR removed project.logs.writer from keystore-proxy SA (PR #4217). that would prevent the proxy from writing audit entries. attaching diff excerpt:```
- roles/logging.logWriter -> keystore-proxy@project.iam
+ removed
```
nina: Confirmed: service account keystore-proxy@redwood.iam lost logging write role in commit abcdef. repro on my laptop with that SA shows no audit events.
marco: Short-term mitigation: re-grant logging writer and restart the proxy. Longer-term: add an automated test asserting decrypt calls generate audit events, and add a policy guard so roles/logging.logWriter can't be removed from critical SAs without a check.
alyssa: Also propose a canary metric: decrypt:audit_emitted ratio (emitted/total) + an alert if < 90% for 5m.
sec-bot: sec-bot: Recommendation — rotate keystore-proxy token after role fix and force re-auth to flush any stale creds. Also schedule an expedited audit of related SAs.
jordan: For private/on-prem customers we should add optional local-audit-forwarder that duplicates events to customer SIEM (with opt-in/privacy guardrails). avoids single point of failure on our central sink.
sam: I'll open a quick PR to re-add role + restart steps, and a follow-up PR for the test and metric. assigning rollback plan to @marco.
marco: :thumbsup: I'll run the rollback in staging then prod if green. ETA ~2h.
nina: Filed incident INC-2025-034 and linked the staging traces (https://incidents.redwood/INC-2025-034). Proposal in the ticket: immediate role restore + metric + unit test + policy guard.
marco: If we can't restore role fast enough, fallback is to re-route decrypts to the HSM pool that logs at the KMS layer — heavier but logs at source.
alyssa: Also add a short runbook step: on audit gap detect, check SA roles -> if missing, reapply and restart proxy, then verify request_id shows up in SIEM.
sec-bot: sec-bot: Also recommend postmortem focusing on change control: how did infra PR remove a critical role without security sign-off?
nina: Thanks — will sync in 30 for immediate fixes.
alyssa: Thanks all, will own the metric/alert work and post status here.
